health_benefits: Rich in alpha-tocopherol (Vitamin E), magnesium, and monounsaturated fats; lowers LDL cholesterol, regulates blood sugar, and enhances skin health.
intake_methods: Soak 5-6 almonds overnight, peel and eat in the morning; or consume raw/dry-roasted as a midday snack.
Vitamin_Explanation: Almonds are a notable dietary source of vitamin E, an antioxidant vitamin.

health_benefits: High-density plant protein, resveratrol, and niacin (B3); supports muscle synthesis, heart health, and sustained satiety.
intake_methods: Boiled, dry-roasted without salt, prepared as natural peanut butter, or added to traditional sundal and poha.
Vitamin_Explanation: Peanuts provide exceptionally high levels of niacin (vitamin B3), essential for cellular energy production and DNA repair.

health_benefits: Abundant in copper, magnesium, and oleic acid; promotes red blood cell formation, supports bone integrity, and protects eye tissue.
intake_methods: Eat a small handful raw or lightly toasted, blend into dairy-free curry gravies, or mix into trail mixes.
Vitamin_Explanation: Cashews are a distinctive nut source of vitamin K, which works alongside magnesium and copper for bone integrity.

health_benefits: Outstanding dietary source of plant Omega-3 fatty acids (ALA) and polyphenols; boosts cognitive health, reduces arterial inflammation, and supports heart function.
intake_methods: Eat 2-3 soaked walnut halves on an empty stomach in the morning, crush over salads, or blend into morning smoothies.
Vitamin_Explanation: Walnuts provide vitamin B6 and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA Omega-3), supporting neural communication and brain health.

health_benefits: Rich in lutein, zeaxanthin, and Vitamin B6; supports ocular wellness, aids neurotransmitter synthesis, and improves lipid profiles.
intake_methods: Snack on a small handful (unsalted, in-shell), chop over oatmeal and desserts, or add to grain bowls.
Vitamin_Explanation: Pistachios are one of the most vitamin B6-dense foods in existence, providing key support for hemoglobin synthesis.

health_benefits: High in Vitamin E, selenium, and phytosterols; shields cell membranes from oxidative stress and promotes cardiovascular wellness.
intake_methods: Eat raw or lightly roasted, sprinkle over salads and yogurt bowls, or blend into seed butter.
Vitamin_Explanation: Sunflower seeds are a phenomenal natural source of vitamin E, offering superior cellular lipid protection.

health_benefits: Dense in bioavailable zinc, magnesium, and tryptophan; strengthens immune defenses, supports prostate health, and improves sleep quality.
intake_methods: Dry-roast with a pinch of rock salt, add to granola and trail mixes, or sprinkle over soups.
Vitamin_Explanation: Pumpkin seeds provide abundant vitamin K, zinc, and magnesium for musculoskeletal and prostate health.

health_benefits: Richest plant source of ALA Omega-3 and lignans; reduces blood pressure, supports hormonal balance, and enhances bowel regularity.
intake_methods: Grind freshly before consumption and add 1 tablespoon to warm water, curd, smoothies, or atta dough.
Vitamin_Explanation: Flax seeds supply rich amounts of thiamine (vitamin B1) to assist cellular energy conversion from dietary fats.

health_benefits: Exceptional soluble mucilage fiber and ALA Omega-3; creates slow-digesting satiety gel, stabilizes insulin, and hydrates colon.
intake_methods: Soak 1-2 teaspoons in water, coconut water, or milk for 15-20 minutes until gelled; add to puddings or juices.
Vitamin_Explanation: Chia seeds provide substantial niacin (vitamin B3) alongside soluble mucilage fiber and plant omega-3s.

health_benefits: Unrivaled calcium density and sesamin lignans; builds bone mineral density, protects liver function, and supports cartilage health.
intake_methods: Lightly roast and add to spice powders (idli podi), sprinkle over stir-fries, or prepare traditional ellu urundai.
Vitamin_Explanation: Sesame seeds are rich in thiamine (vitamin B1) and sesamin lignans, supporting nervous and cardiovascular functions.
